title: A strategy is a diagnosis, a guiding policy and coherent action — not a list of goals

videos.script: Ask ten companies for their technical strategy and most of them will send you a list. {{title}} Migrate to microservices. Reach four nines of availability. Cut the cloud bill by a fifth. Every line sounds sensible. None of them says what is actually wrong, or what the company will stop doing to fix it. {{list}} This course uses Richard Rumelt's definition instead. A strategy is a diagnosis of the challenge. Then a guiding policy for dealing with it. Then a few actions that support each other. {{kernel}} We follow one company all the way through. Coreto sells tickets for theatres, concert halls and festivals. Its engineers are asked for a strategy, and their first draft is exactly that list. {{coreto}} By the end of this lesson you can tell a strategy from a list of goals. You will also have a spreadsheet ready on your own computer, because from lesson five on, most of the arguments in this course are made in money. {{sheet}}
